quotes.text: Your account might be reviewed after activation to confirm eligibility.
The voucher expires after 3 days by default, configurable from 0–60 days.
This number identifies the voucher, but it isn’t a processor transaction ID.

old_evidence.text: You’ll receive payment confirmation after 1 business day, and funds will be available for payout 2 business days after payment confirmation.
Boleto payments can’t be refunded. You need to create a separate process to credit customers who require a refund.
The amount for a single Boleto must be at least 5.00 BRL and no more than 49,999.99 BRL.

findings: The November capture retains the voucher payment sequence but expands the overview: Brazil merchant/platform and customer, BRL domestic presentment, B2B/B2C, no extra MCC requirement, possible postactivation eligibility review, and BRL 5.00–49,999.99 range (new raw lines 7-40). The May capture documents BR customers/accounts, BRL and the amount range but lacks the new eligibility qualifiers (old raw lines 8-10, 14-32, 54-58, 114-116). Current source lines 13-23 has the geography and range but no eligibility-review boundary.

The new capability matrix says recurring, Billing, Invoicing, Customer Portal, Connect, SetupIntents and PaymentIntents with setup_future_usage are supported, but off-session payments are not (new raw lines 41-92). Therefore source lines 29-35 and concept lines 51-55 must not be read as automatic off-session collection: even recurring Boleto requires customer payment of each voucher. The old overview only has yes/no recurring and broad product support (old raw lines 30-40, 60-70).

New raw lines 110-126 specifies contact and tax ID collection, hosted voucher number/PDF, default 3-day expiry configurable 0–60 days, and asynchronous payment confirmation typically next business day. Voucher creation and 'instant provisional access' at new raw line 12 are not paid status or settlement. Old raw lines 72-85 has only a graphical four-step flow; source lines 13, 21 make confirmation sound fixed rather than up-to/typical.

New raw lines 128-136 adds a distinct customer-visible voucher number at payment_intent.next_action.boleto_display_details.number, explicitly not a processor transaction ID, and says latest_charge.payment_method_details.boleto has no processor transaction ID. Full statement_descriptor is request-level or account fallback; suffix only applies to cards; bank display may vary or omit it. Connect destination-charge descriptor follows platform without on_behalf_of and connected account with it, subject to legacy API-version behavior. These identity and account/version qualifications are absent from source lines 11-39 and old raw lines 1-116.

New raw lines 13-14 uses 'Up to 1 business day' confirmation and 'Up to 2 business days (T+2)' settlement, without defining the settlement clock. Old raw line 10 says funds available for payout two business days after payment confirmation. Current source lines 13, 21 and concept line 45 conflate or simplify these as 'T+2 payout' after confirmation. Preserve the dated old wording and do not silently equate settlement, payout availability and payout arrival.

Current source frontmatter lines 1-9 lacks canonical_url and only names the May raw; a proposed update must add exact https://docs.stripe.com/payments/boleto and both dated raw files. Current source line 25 says no refund exceptions, while both captures support only that Stripe Boleto full/partial refunds are unavailable (old raw lines 50-52, 110-112; new raw lines 57-59); separate credit process is old historical guidance, not a claim that all remedial credit is impossible.

The discoverable Stripe index line 374 and voucher concept source route line 114 repeat '1-day confirmation, T+2 payout'; concept line 45 and mapped source lines 13, 21 do likewise. New raw lines 13-14 instead say up-to-one-business-day confirmation and up-to-two-business-day settlement with no stated anchor, whereas old raw line 10 dates payout availability to two business days after confirmation. Warn at these reciprocal routes rather than silently promoting old payout wording to November guidance.

A separate May 2026 subscription guide example creates a Subscription with collection_method: charge_automatically and off_session: true (raw/stripe-boleto-subscription-2025.md lines 331-350; source-stripe-boleto-subscription.md lines 28-36). Its invoice guide says even charge_automatically still requires the customer to pay each Boleto voucher (raw/stripe-boleto-invoices-2025.md lines 274-284; source-stripe-boleto-invoices.md lines 13-25). The November overview says Boleto off-session payments are unsupported (new raw line 92). These statements have different object/action scopes; do not infer the old Subscription creation example authorizes off-session Boleto payment today or that the new overview proves the dated Subscription request invalid.

Current source line 27 and concept line 49 say Stripe handles bank-side irregularities, but old raw line 108 and new raw line 66 say Stripe contacts the merchant with next steps. Correct the agency/action wording while retaining no standard customer dispute or chargeback.
substantive_changes: The new capture adds account eligibility/review, domestic-only and no-MCC qualifiers plus a detailed capability matrix including the important SetupIntent/setup_future_usage versus no-off-session distinction (old raw lines 12-70; new raw lines 16-92).

The new capture adds exact hosted-voucher expiry and async flow, statement-descriptor account rules, and an explicit voucher-number versus processor-ID boundary (old raw lines 72-85; new raw lines 110-136).

The new capture changes timing wording from confirmation after one business day and payout availability two business days after confirmation to confirmation up to one business day and settlement up to two business days T+2, with no explicit common anchor (old raw line 10; new raw lines 12-14, 124-126).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May 7, 2026 old raw line 10 as a dated statement about payout availability after confirmation; the November 7, 2026 page gives settlement timing without defining the same anchor. Retain both raw files and their dates.

Old raw lines 106-116 expressly described a separate credit process, bank-side irregularities, and amount limits. New raw lines 38-40, 57-66 confirm limits and standard refunds/disputes unavailability, but do not itself specify a replacement credit process; keep the old advice dated.

The May 2026 subscription guide's Subscription creation example sets collection_method: charge_automatically and off_session: true (raw/stripe-boleto-subscription-2025.md lines 331-350). Preserve it as dated request-example evidence, not an off-session Boleto payment guarantee; the May invoices guide explicitly requires customer voucher payment even with charge_automatically (raw/stripe-boleto-invoices-2025.md line 284), and November overview excludes off-session payments (new raw line 92).
conflicts: Old raw line 10 and current source lines 13, 21 and concept line 45 use payout availability two business days after confirmation; new raw line 14 says settlement up to two business days T+2. The timings have different labels and unstated new anchor, requiring reciprocal dated warning.

Source line 25 says 'No exceptions'; the captures only establish Stripe Boleto full/partial refunds unsupported and old raw lines 110-112 say merchants need a separate credit process. Scope the source claim to the Stripe refund capability.

Source lines 29-35 and concept lines 51-55 emphasize recurring/setup support; new raw line 92 explicitly excludes off-session payments. Preserve that distinction and the concept's customer-pays-voucher caveat.

Source and concept line 45 omit new provisional-access, eligibility-review and asynchronous confirmation qualifications (new raw lines 12-14, 22, 124-126); neither voucher receipt nor provisional access proves funds settled.

Stripe index line 374 and concept source route line 114 repeat dated fixed confirmation/T+2 payout labels even though new raw lines 13-14 distinguish up-to confirmation and settlement; old raw line 10 supplies the older payout-after-confirmation anchor.

Dated Subscription creation example uses off_session: true with charge_automatically (raw/stripe-boleto-subscription-2025.md lines 331-350), while new raw line 92 excludes off-session Boleto payments; the invoice guide requires customer voucher payment (raw/stripe-boleto-invoices-2025.md line 284). This is an apparent cross-page parameter/path conflict, not proof of successful off-session payment or invalid Subscription request.
Source line 27 and concept line 49 overstate Stripe's action as handling bank irregularities; both raw captures say Stripe contacts the merchant with next steps (old raw line 108; new raw line 66).
unresolved_questions: The new overview does not define whether its T+2 settlement clock starts at voucher payment or confirmation, nor a merchant-specific payout schedule (new raw lines 12-14 versus old raw line 10).
The overview does not prove activation, customer eligibility, successful voucher payment, payout arrival, or API-version behavior of a given Connect account (new raw lines 18-24, 124-136).

The new overview's links to quickstarts, samples, subscription/invoice and manual Boleto setup are navigation; their detailed rules are not established merely by those links (new raw lines 93-108, 140-142).

Whether the May subscription example's off_session: true remains accepted today, or how that Subscription creation parameter relates to November's no-off-session-payment matrix, cannot be resolved by these captures; keep Subscription creation, invoice collection, and customer payment as separate transitions (subscription raw lines 331-350; invoice raw line 284; new overview line 92).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/boleto, Boleto is a Brazil domestic BRL voucher method: a BR merchant or Connect platform offers it to a BR customer, who provides contact and tax ID details, receives a hosted voucher, then pays before expiry through a bank, ATM, agency or portal. The new capture states provisional access, possible postactivation review, default three-day voucher expiry, asynchronous confirmation typically next business day, and a separate up-to-T+2 settlement label; voucher issuance is not payment success (new raw lines 7-40, 110-136). Recurring, setup_future_usage and SetupIntents are listed, but off-session Boleto payments are excluded (new raw lines 41-92). The old capture gave broader yes/no properties and payout availability two business days after confirmation (old raw lines 8-70). A dated subscription guide has off_session: true on a Subscription creation request, yet its invoice guide still requires customer voucher payment; this does not establish an off-session Boleto charge today. source-stripe-boleto.md preserves older geography, limits and refund restrictions but omits the new eligibility, lifecycle and voucher-number versus processor-ID boundary; its timing and bank-irregularity wording need qualification (source lines 11-35).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/boleto, substantive additions are the Brazil account review and domestic eligibility matrix, no-off-session restriction despite setup/recurring support, hosted voucher expiry, and customer-visible Boleto number versus absent processor transaction ID, with Connect descriptor ownership dependent on on_behalf_of and legacy API version (old raw lines 12-85; new raw lines 16-136). The new up-to confirmation and settlement labels must stay distinct from old payout-availability-after-confirmation wording (old raw line 10; new raw lines 12-14); source-stripe-boleto.md, Stripe index line 374, voucher concept line 45 and its source route line 114 need reciprocal dated warnings. The May subscription guide's off_session: true on Subscription creation apparently conflicts with new overview line 92, yet the invoice guide says customer voucher payment is still required: neither capture proves a current successful off-session Boleto payment or invalidates the dated Subscription request. Both captures say Stripe contacts the merchant about bank-side irregularities, contrary to the mapped source's 'Stripe handles' claim. Headings, flow presentation and quickstart links are presentation/navigation rather than integration proof. Retain May provenance, add the November raw/canonical URL, scope refund 'no exceptions,' and do not treat voucher display, provisional access, SetupIntent, PaymentIntent request or browser flow as successful payment, settlement or payout.
